name: Stinson Junior (S / R / SR)
summary: Late-1920s and early-1930s four-seat cabin monoplane, one of the first with a fully enclosed cabin. The Junior R introduced low stub wings to carry the gear.

wings: High wing braced by struts on each side
Outrigger landing gear braced against the wing struts
engines: Single radial engine, often uncowled with cylinders exposed
fuselage: Fixed tailwheel gear; the Junior R has a low stub wing carrying the gear

tellTales: Vintage cabin high-wing with a radial engine and struts bracing both wing and gear
Exposed or lightly cowled radial nose
Tall fixed gear braced to the wing struts

confusedWith.howToTell: The Reliant (1933) is the cleaner, more refined cowled successor; the Junior is earlier and boxier, often with an exposed radial.
The Robin is a three-seater with a pylon and a different wing support; the Junior has a four-seat cabin and a full strut brace.
The Waco cabin biplane has two sets of wings; the Junior is a high-wing monoplane.
